thread_text:
pagerduty: INCIDENT: High error rate and 99th pct latency spike observed for inference endpoints in eu-west-az4. Pager triggered (severity: p1).
incident-bot: Automated correlation: spike appears to originate from high concurrent seq-length heavy requests to model 'rw-13b-v2', autoscaler crossing scale-up threshold. Suggested runbook: /runbooks/az-throughput-surge.
alex: Ack. I'm on-call and looking. First check: are we seeing CPU/GPU saturations or queueing?
maria: I'm pulling gpu metrics now — nv_top shows sustained 98% utilization on GPU 0-3 for the affected pool. Memory shortfalls reported on GPU 1.
jin: Checking request queue depth — redis-queue length jumped to ~11k for az4-inference-queue, normally ~200. That's causing queuing latency.
sanjay: Noted. Any recent rollouts in az4?
alex: No prod rollouts in last 2 hours. Canary was fine.
incident-bot: Alert escalation: Unacked >2m. Notifying senior on-call.
kelsey: On it, paging infra-sre team. Suggest activating regional fallback routing to eu-west-az2 while we mitigate.
ops-oncall: Agreed. Initiating routing policy: route 40% traffic to az2, 60% to az4 for gradual failover. Command run: `infractl routing apply --region eu-west --policy gradual-az2-fallback --weight 40`
maria: Confirmed route change applied, propagated to edge within 90s. Monitoring for errors.
alex: Parallel mitigation: scale up the az4 pool by adding 8 gpus (scale-group: az4-burst). Command: ```
kubectl scale --replicas=10 deployment/az4-inference-pool -n inference
# or
infractl scale pool az4-burst --add-gpus 8
```
jin: Autoscaler logs show throttling due to quota on az4. Manual burst succeeded but some pods are stuck in Pending with message `failed to allocate GPU: quota exceeded`.
sanjay: I've opened a quota increase with cloud-provider, but that'll take time. Can we drain some low-priority workloads?
kelsey: Yes — switching background eval jobs to queue 'low-priority' and evicting non-critical caches. Command: `infractl job reprioritize --tag eval --priority low`
alex: Eviction started. Also enabling aggressive KV prefix caching to reduce repeated generation costs: `runtimectl cache enable-prefix --ttl 300s`.
incident-bot: System note: prefix cache hit-rate target applied to az4 routing.
maria: After routing change + evictions, queue depth dropped from 11k -> 2.1k in 6 minutes. GPU mem pressure eased on GPU 1; error rate starting to fall.
jin: 99th latency still elevated (~1.8s -> baseline 200ms) but trending down. No customer-facing errors except elevated latency for a subset of large-sequence requests.
sanjay: Can we enable graceful degrade for long-seq jobs (max_tokens cap) to protect p95? Suggested policy: enforce `max_new_tokens=512` for non-SLA tenants temporarily.
alex: Pushed runtime policy for non-enterprise tenants. Command: `runtimectl policy set --name short-seq-fallback --max-new-tokens 512 --match non_sla`
kelsey: Notifying account managers for customers with high throughput to expect transient latency for long inputs. Draft message: "We're seeing a throughput surge in eu-west-az4 impacting long-sequence inference latency. We've routed traffic and applied mitigations; degradation is partial. Will update in 15 minutes."
ops-oncall: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by alex, escalated to infra-sre (kelsey) and platform-eng (sanjay).
incident-bot: Escalation timer: 15m until auto-escalate to SRE director if not resolved.
maria: At T+18m, overall error rate back to normal (5xx = baseline). 99th latency improved to ~430ms.
jin: Queue depth stable ~220. All new pods in az4 are Running. Remaining tail latency due to a small subset of >8k token requests still routed to az4 (enterprise pinned).
sanjay: For pinned enterprise workloads, we should proactively failover those customers if SLA allows. Recommending manual customer-level failover to az2 for 3 tenants. Who can approve?
kelsey: I authorize failover for tenant IDs 9001, 9067, 9122 (they accepted emergency routing in contract). Initiating per-tenant route flip.
alex: Done. Those tenants now hitting az2. Latency for them dropped to baseline within 90s.
incident-bot: NOTE: failover activation logged: `failover:manual:tenants:9001,9067,9122` (audit id: af-233450-01).
maria: Monitoring: overall 99th now 210ms. Good.
jin: Closing mitigation loop: revert temporary short-seq policy and requeue evicted jobs to low-priority after sustained healthy metrics.
ops-oncall: Preparing incident summary for postmortem: root cause preliminary: sudden burst of long-sequence concurrent requests overloaded az4 pool, autoscaler hit cloud quota, and blocking scale-up. Contributing factors: no pre-configured tenant-level overflow routing, low-priority job eviction not automated.
kelsey: Action items: 1) automated tenant-level overflow rules 2) quota alert earlier in autoscaler path 3) scripted burst pool provisioning + pre-authorized cloud quota runway. Owners: platform-eng (sanjay), infra-sre (kelsey), runtime (alex). Due: 2 weeks.
alex: Handing off to next on-call: @ops-oncall take over from me, I'll add notes in the incident doc.
ops-oncall: Ack handoff. I'll continue watching for 2 hours.
incident-bot: Incident resolved condition met. Closing pager. Root cause ticket: INC-233450-az4-throughput created.
pagerduty: Resolved: Incident INC-233450-az4-throughput marked resolved by alex.

# reactions: :white_check_mark: on routing change, :rocket: on tenant failover, :eyes: on postmortem notes
